question.note: Spillover onto perceptions (Q1) and representation (Q3), and whether a counter-narrative mitigates it (Q2).

central_claim.note: Gives all three parts: harm to perceptions, improved representation, and the counter-narrative's near-removal of the harm ('vastly ameliorated', abstract).

evidence.note: Survey experiment with Democrats via Prolific (E1 without pre-registration or dates). Three arms without identities or N (part of E2). Indices for perceptions, representation and ad support (E4 minus officials' motives).

key_findings.note: Counter-narrative shown first vs ad alone; magnitude only in the quote.
Names quality of Democratic representation and public-serving motives, both increased vs control (Table 3).

theoretical_positioning.note: Social categorization theory with the salient-exemplar mechanism. No T4 (no statement that the study tests the theory's prediction on the ad).
